BURHAN:v1p206/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p206/r1.speaker: عائشة
BURHAN:v1p206/r1.claim: The beginning-of-revelation report in al-Bukhari, explicitly authenticated by al-Hakim from Aisha, establishes اقرأ as the first revelation; Muslim gives it through “He taught man what he did not know.”
BURHAN:v1p206/r1.anchor: وأخرجه الحاكم فى مستدركه من حديث عائشة رضى الله عنها صريحا وقال صحيح الإسناد

ITQAN:v1p75/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p75/r1.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
ITQAN:v1p75/r1.claim: Ubayd b. ʿUmayr says Gabriel brought the Prophet a silk sheet and told him to recite; he identifies the opening of al-ʿAlaq as the first sura sent down.
ITQAN:v1p75/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن أشتة في كتاب المصاحف عن عبيد بن عمير قال جاء جبريل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بنمط فقال اقرأ

ITQAN:v1p75/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p75/r2.speaker: الزهري
ITQAN:v1p75/r2.claim: Al-Zuhrī recounts that while the Prophet was at Ḥirāʾ, an angel brought a silk sheet inscribed with the opening verses of al-ʿAlaq.
ITQAN:v1p75/r2.anchor: وأخرج عن الزهري أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بحراء إذ أتى ملك بنمط من ديباج فيه مكتوب

BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r6.claim: God taught by means of the pen while teaching the Prophet without writing; others explain the phrase as teaching handwriting and script through the cutting nib.
BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r6.anchor: أي علم ما علم بواسطة القلم لا غيره

BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r7.claim: Teaching writing is a favor to humanity; knowledge is a catch and writing its tether, and the poem urges writers to leave only what they would wish to see at Judgment.
BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r7.anchor: وفيه امتنان على الإنسان بتعليم علم الخط والكتابة بالقلم ولذلك قيل العلم صيد

BURSEVI:v10p364/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p364/r1.speaker: كعب الأحبار
BURSEVI:v10p364/r1.claim: Kaab al-Ahbar reports that Adam wrote Arabic, Syriac, and all books in clay three hundred years before death, later recovered by Idris; Idris invented sand writing, Tahmurth Persian writing, and Joseph papyrus.
BURSEVI:v10p364/r1.anchor: قال كعب الأحبار أول من وضع الكتاب العربي والسرياني والكتب كلها آدم عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v10p364/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p364/r2.speaker: السيوطي
BURSEVI:v10p364/r2.claim: Al-Suyuti says God commanded the first created pen to record everything destined until Judgment Day, beginning with God's promise to forgive whoever repents.
BURSEVI:v10p364/r2.anchor: قال السيوطي رحمه الله أول ما خلق الله القلم قال له اكتب ما هو كائن

QASHANI:96:3-8/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:96:3-8/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:96:3-8/r2.claim: The pen is the supreme first spirit, the means through which God taught.
QASHANI:96:3-8/r2.anchor: القلم الأعلى الذي هو الروح الأول الأعظم

QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r8.claim: God taught people what they did not know, including both necessary and acquired knowledge.
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r8.anchor: علمهم ما لم يعلموا : الضروري ، والكسبي

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450/r1.claim: Qatada calls the pen a great divine blessing, without which religion would not stand and livelihood would not be sound.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : الذي علم بالقلم قال : القلم نعمة من الله عظيمة ، لولا القلم لم يقم دين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r3.claim: Aisha narrates in the two Sahihs that Gabriel came to Muhammad in Hira, commanded him three times, embraced him forcefully each time, then recited the opening through 'what he did not know.'
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r3.anchor: وفي حديث ( الصحيحين ) عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قولها فيه : ( حتى جاءه الحق وهو في غار حراء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r4.claim: Aisha's narration is directly from the Prophet; her account that he returned trembling with the passage means he retained and recited what had been dictated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r4.anchor: فهذا الحديث روته عائشة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لقولها قال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r5.claim: Khadija's request that Waraqa hear him further indicates Muhammad recited the revealed passage immediately; Gabriel's repeated command repeated God's wording to accustom him to reading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r5.anchor: وهذا ينبىء بأن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عندما قيل له بعد الفطة الثالثة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r2.claim: The clause is a new explanatory statement: Rabbuka is subject, with either 'who taught by the pen' or 'taught humanity what it did not know' as predicate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r2.anchor: و { ربك } مبتدأ وخبره إما { الذي علم بالقلم } وإما جملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r3.claim: Without Aisha's revelation report, the statement answers Muhammad's presumed question about reading without literacy: the one who taught writing can teach what he does not know.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r3.anchor: كيف أقرأ وأنا لا أحسن القراءة والكتابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r4.claim: With the hadith, the passage answers his 'I cannot read': God can teach by dictation, instruction, or inspiration, just as He taught Adam the names without literacy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r4.anchor: إذ العلم بالقراءة يحصل بوسائل أخرى مثل الإملاء والتلقين والإلهام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r5.claim: Repeating 'your Lord' instead of using a pronoun stresses the care already implied in 'recite in your Lord's name' and marks reading as a special gift of lordship; it also leads into al-Akram.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r5.anchor: فعدل عن الإضمار لتأكيد ما يشعر به { ربك } من العناية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r6.claim: Al-Akram intensifies generosity rather than comparing God with another; generosity is giving benefit, and God's favors begin with creation and its sustaining provision.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r6.anchor: ووصف { الأكرم } مصوغ للدلالة على قوة الاتصاف بالكرم وليس مصوغا للمفاضلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r7.claim: The opening five verses gather divine attributes: lordship implies existence and oneness, creation and teaching indicate acts, and al-Akram entails perfection and freedom from deficiency.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r7.anchor: وقد جمعت هذه الآيات الخمس من أول السورة أصول الصفات الإلاهية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r1.claim: The two objects of 'taught by the pen' are omitted, understood as teaching writers or teaching people to write; Arabs prized literacy and associated it with scriptural communities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r1.anchor: ومفعولا { علم بالقلم } محذوفان دل عليهما قوله : { بالقلم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r2.speaker: أبو حية النميري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r2.claim: Abu Hayya's line about a Jew's hand supports the association of writing with Jews and skilled script.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r2.anchor: كما قال أبو حية النميري : كما خط الكتاب بكف يوما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r3.claim: A second poem boasts of learning writing though its speaker says he is no writer; writing first appeared among Arabs in Anbar, then reached Hijaz through Harb ibn Umayya, who learned from Aslam ibn Sidra, taught by Muramir ibn Murra; Himyar earlier used Musnad.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r3.anchor: وذكر أن ظهور الخط في العرب أول ما كان عند أهل الأنبار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r4.claim: Placing 'who taught by the pen' between subject and predicate reassures the Prophet that the one who taught writing can teach him recitation though he cannot write.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r4.anchor: وتخصيص هذه الصلة بالذكر وجعلها معترضة بين المبتدإ والخبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r5.claim: The pen is a sharpened reed used to draw ink on paper; the discussion also recalls pens cast to decide who would care for Mary.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r5.anchor: والقلم : شظية من قصب ترقق وتثقف وتبرى بالسكين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r5.claim: The initial command and reference to pen teaching imply that Muhammad remained unlettered, an attribute completing the Qur'an's miracle, as another verse states.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r5.anchor: وفي الاقتصار على أمر الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بالقراءة ثم إخباره بأن الله علم الإنسان بالقلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r6.claim: These are the final five verses of the passage first revealed at Hira; the following discussion on verses 6–10 begins a new subject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r6.anchor: وهذه آخر الخمس الآيات التي هي أول ما أنزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r3.claim: Teaching through the pen is a blessing to humanity, a great means of communication and of preserving knowledge.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r3.anchor: ثم عدد تعالى نعمة الكتاب بالقلم على الناس وهي موضع عبرة وأعظم منفعة في المخاطبات وتخليد المعارف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#2/r1.claim: God taught people to write with the pen.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r1.claim: These first Qur'anic verses were the first mercy and blessing to people, reminding them of creation from a clot and God's generosity in teaching what people did not know.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r1.anchor: فأول شيء [نزل] (2) من القرآن هذه الآيات الكريمات المباركات (3) وهن أول رحمة رحم الله بها العباد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r2.claim: God honored humanity with knowledge, the distinction by which Adam surpassed the angels; knowledge exists mentally, verbally, and in writing, with writing entailing the other two but not vice versa, hence the mention of the pen.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r2.anchor: وفيها التنبيه على ابتداء خلق الإنسان من علقة، وأن من كرمه تعالى أن علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم، فشرفه وكرمه بالعلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r3.claim: An early maxim says to bind knowledge by writing it down.

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan and has seventeen verses.

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r10.speaker: عائشة ومجاهد وعطاء بن يسار
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r10.claim: One report says the first revelation from the Qur'an was Iqraʾ bismi rabbik.
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r10.anchor: قيل: أول ما نزل من القرآن: (اقرأ باسم ربك)، عن عائشة، ومجاهد، وعطاء بن يسار.

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r11.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r11.claim: Another report says the first five verses descended first, while the rest of the surah came later; a similar report is attributed to ʿĀʾisha.
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r11.anchor: وقيل: أول ما نزل منها خمس آيات إلى قوله: (ما لم يعلم)، ثم نزل باقي السورة بعد ذلك

JISHUMI:v10p7477/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r15.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r15.claim: Teaching by the pen means writing, which benefits religion and worldly life through preserving knowledge, preventing forgetting, and recording needs.
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r15.anchor: علم الخط والكتابة الذي فيها النفع العظيم فيما يتعلق بالدين والدنيا

JISHUMI:v10p7477/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r16.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r16.claim: Qatāda calls the pen a great blessing from God; without it religion and livelihood would not be established.
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r16.anchor: قال قتادة: القلم نعمة من الله تعالى عظيمة، لولاه لم يقم دين، ولم يصلح عيش،

JISHUMI:v10p7477/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r17.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r17.claim: The pen may mean God's speech written in the Preserved Tablet, read by angels and conveyed to people.
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r17.anchor: أراد علم كلامه بأن كتب لهم في اللوح المحفوظ حتى قرأه الملائكة وبلغوه الناس

JISHUMI:v10p7477/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r18.claim: Other interpretations mean the physical writing pen, all religious and legal knowledge, all human learning from God, or the necessary sciences and reasoning that complete the intellect.
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r18.anchor: وقيل: أراد نفس القلم الذي يتوصل به إلى الكتابة علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم من أمور دينه

JISHUMI:v10p7477/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r19.claim: The author says the first explanation is strongest: God taught humanity by the pen what it had not known, enabling writing, preservation, and instruction.
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r19.anchor: والأول الوجه، وقيل: علم بالقلم من أمور دينه ودنياه ما لم يعلمه قبل ذلك

JISHUMI:v10p7477/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r20.claim: Further views say God taught Adam the names and his descendants inherited this learning, or that “the human” here is Muḥammad, as in “He taught you what you did not know.”
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r20.anchor: وقيل: علم آدم الأسماء، ثم صار ذلك في أولاده، والإنسان آدم، وقيل: الإنسان محمد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r7.claim: Teaching writing and what people did not know is the highest sign of God's generosity, moving humanity from ignorance to knowledge.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r7.anchor: حيث قال : الأكرم { الذي علم بالقلم * علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r8.claim: Writing preserves disciplines, wisdom, early reports, and revealed books; without it religion and worldly affairs would not stand.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r8.anchor: ونبه على فضل علم الكتابة لما فيه من المنافع العظيمة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p782/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p782/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p782/r1.claim: A poem from an unnamed author describes the pen's dark lines and ink as paths continued by white strokes, offering evidence about writing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p782/r1.anchor: ورواقم رقش كمثل أراقم … قطف الخطا نيالة أقصى المدى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p782/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p782/r2.speaker: ابن الزبير
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p782/r2.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reads the phrase as teaching writing with the pen.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p782/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير : ( علم الخط بالقلم )

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r13.claim: God taught the writer to write with a pen.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r13.anchor: الذي علم بالقلم } أي علم الكاتب أن يكتب بالقلم , وسمي قلما

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r14.claim: Qalam is named from cutting, as in trimming a fingernail.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r14.anchor: وسمي قلما لأنى يقلم أي يقطع , ومنه تقليم الظفر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r15.speaker: ابن عمر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r15.claim: God created four things with His hand and told the rest of creation Be, and it was: the Pen, Throne, Garden of Eden, and Adam.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r15.anchor: وروى مجاهد عن ابن عمر قال : خلق الله تعالى أربعة أشياء بيده ثم قال لسائر الخلق : كن , فكان

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r16.speaker: كعب الأحبار
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r16.claim: Adam was the one taught by the pen because he was the first to write.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r16.anchor: أحدها : أنه أراد آدم عليه السلام , لأنه أول من كتب , قاله كعب الأحبار .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r17.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r17.claim: Idris was the one taught by the pen because he was the first to write.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r17.anchor: الثاني : إدريس وهو أول من كتب , قاله الضحاك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r18.claim: The verse can mean everyone who writes with a pen, since writing comes only through God's teaching; this joins the blessings of creation and instruction.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r18.anchor: الثالث : أنه أراد كل من كتب بالقلم لأنه ما علم إلا بتعليم الله له , وجمع بذلك بين نعمته تعالى عليه

MUQATIL:96:1-8/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:96:1-8/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:96:1-8/r3.claim: The pen passage means God taught writing and taught the human being the Qur'an, knowledge previously unknown.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#7/r1.claim: God taught writing by means of the pen.

NAHHAS:v5p261/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p261/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p261/r8.claim: Alladhī is an adjective modifying the first alladhī.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r1.claim: Teaching by the pen means teaching writing; Qatada calls the pen a great divine favor, for religion, livelihood, recorded sciences, wisdom, past reports, and revealed books depend on writing.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r1.anchor: يعني الخط والكتابة أي علم الإنسان الخط بالقلم

QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r2.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r2.claim: Qatada says the pen is a tremendous blessing from God, without which religion would not stand and life would not be sound.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r2.anchor: وروى سعيد عن قتادة قال: القلم نعمة من الله تعالى عظيمة، لولا ذلك لم يقم دين،

QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r3.claim: The verse highlights the value of writing, through which sciences, judgments, inherited reports, and revealed books are recorded, and explains qalam from cutting, as in clipping a nail.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r3.anchor: وسمي قلما لأنه يقلم أي يقطع، ومنه تقليم الظفر.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r4.speaker: الشعراء المحدثون
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r4.claim: A modern poet compares an ink-stained pen tip to an old man courting a young woman and says the pen deserves reverence because pages written with it rise to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r4.anchor: وقال بعض الشعراء المحدثين يصف القلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r5.claim: Ibn Umar asked the Prophet whether he could write down what he heard; the Prophet said yes and cited God's teaching by the pen.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r5.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن عمر قال: يا رسول الله، أأكتب ما أسمع منك من الحديث؟

QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r6.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r6.claim: Mujahid transmits from Ibn Umar that God made four things by His hand before saying Be to other creatures: the pen, Throne, Eden, and Adam.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r6.anchor: وروى مجاهد عن ابن عمر قال: خلق الله عز وجل أربعة أشياء بيده، ثم قال لسائر الحيوان:

QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r7.speaker: كعب الأحبار
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r7.claim: One interpretation says the one taught to write by the pen is Adam, whom Ka'b al-Ahbar calls the first writer.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r7.anchor: أحدها: أنه آدم عليه السلام لأنه أول من كتب، قاله كعب الأحبار.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r8.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r8.claim: A second view identifies Idris as the first writer, as reported by al-Dahhak.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r8.anchor: الثاني: أنه إدريس، وهو أول من كتب. قاله الضحاك.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r9.claim: The third view is general: God taught all who write, gathering the blessings of human creation and instruction into one account.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r9.anchor: الثالث: أنه أدخل كل من كتب بالقلم لأنه ما علم إلا بتعليم الله سبحانه،

QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r10.claim: A sound report from Abu Hurayra says God wrote in a book above the Throne that His mercy overcomes His wrath.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r10.anchor: الثانية: صح عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من حديث أبي هريرة، قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r11.claim: A further Prophetic report says the first thing created was the pen, which was commanded to write all events through the Day of Resurrection in the record above the Throne.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4/r11.anchor: وثبت عنه عليه السلام أنه قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports that after forty-two nights an angel shapes the fetus, forms its senses and body, records sex, lifespan, and provision, then departs with the written decree; the Qur'an calls guardian angels noble scribes.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r1.anchor: إذا مر بالنطفة ثنتان وأربعون ليلة، بعث الله إليها ملكا فصورها،

QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r2.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r2.claim: The scholars classify three kinds of pens: God's first pen for the decrees, angels' pens for destinies and deeds, and people's pens for speech and practical aims.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r2.anchor: قال علماؤنا: فالأقلام في الأصل ثلاثة: القلم الأول: الذي خلقه الله بيده،

QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r3.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r3.claim: Writing has many virtues as a form of communication, which is one of the distinguishing capacities of human beings.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r3.anchor: وفي الكتابة فضائل جمة. والكتابة من جملة البيان، والبيان مما اختص به الآدمي.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r4.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r4.claim: The scholars say Arabs knew writing less than other peoples, and the Prophet was kept from it so his miracle and proof would be stronger; the discussion is treated in al-Ankabut.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r4.anchor: الثالثة: قال علماؤنا: كانت العرب أقل الخلق معرفة بالكتاب، وأقل العرب معرفة به المصطفى صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r5.claim: A report from Ibn Masud attributes to the Prophet a prohibition on giving women upper rooms or teaching them writing.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r6.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r6.claim: The scholars explain the warning against upper rooms by saying they let women look out at men without providing seclusion, risking mutual temptation; they quote a report that women's good lies in not seeing men or being seen by them.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r6.anchor: قال علماؤنا: وإنما حذرهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذلك، لأن في إسكانهن الغرف تطلعا إلى الرجل

QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r7.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r7.claim: They explain that teaching women writing could enable correspondence with a desired man; writing lets the absent be seen and communicates the inner self without speech, so the Prophet sought to cut off what they regarded as causes of temptation and protect chastity.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:4#2/r7.anchor: وكذلك تعليم الكتابة ربما كانت سببا للفتنة، وذلك إذا علمت الكتابة كتبت إلى من تهوى.

QUTB-ZILAL:96:4/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:4/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:4/r1.claim: The pen remains humanity's broadest and deepest tool for teaching; God knew its value and highlighted it at the opening of the final message, though its full significance was not yet apparent.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:4/r1.anchor: لأن القلم كان وما يزال أوسع وأعمق أدوات التعليم أثرا في حياة الإنسان

QUTB-ZILAL:96:4/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:4/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:4/r2.claim: Since the Prophet could not write with a pen, Qutb argues that the verse's early emphasis on writing confirms that this Qur'an is revelation, not something the Prophet composed.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:4/r2.anchor: هذا مع أن الرسول الذي جاء بها لم يكن كاتبا بالقلم

RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r1.claim: Creation of the clot-grown human provides rational proof of power, wisdom, knowledge, and mercy; teaching by the pen points to revealed rulings known through transmission, so knowledge of lordship precedes and grounds prophethood.
RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى الدلالة العقلية الدالة على كمال القدرة والحكمة والعلم والرحمة

RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r2.claim: The pen may signify writing, which conveys hidden matters, or directly mean teaching people to write; both readings emphasize writing's merit.
RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r2.anchor: أن المراد من القلم الكتابة التي تعرف بها الأمور الغائبة ، وجعل القلم كناية عنها

RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r3.claim: A report has Solomon ask a demon about speech: speech is a passing wind, while writing binds it; the ensuing praise presents the pen as a hunter of knowledge, preserving learning across time.
RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r3.anchor: يروى أن سليمان عليه السلام سأل عفريتا عن الكلام ، فقال : ريح لا يبقى ، قال : فما قيده / قال : الكتابة

RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r4.claim: The pen's silent mark is heard across east and west, makes religion luminous with black ink, and preserves knowledge; unlike the pen, the tongue cannot be replaced by writing.
RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r4.anchor: فكذا القلم لا ينطق ثم يسمع الشرق والفرب ، فسبحانه من قادر بسوادها جعل الدين منورا

SAMIN-DURR:96:4-5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:4-5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:96:4-5/r1.claim: The phrase about teaching by the pen and teaching humanity resembles create/create humanity, so the same grammatical analyses apply.
SAMIN-DURR:96:4-5/r1.anchor: قريب من قوله: " خلق، خلق الإنسان " فلك أن تعيد فيه ما تقدم

TAB:96:3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r2.speaker: author
TAB:96:3/r2.claim: Teaching by the pen means teaching creation writing and script.
TAB:96:3/r2.anchor: الّذِي عَلّمَ بِالقَلَمِ :  خَلْقَه الكتاب والخط

TAB:96:3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB:96:3/r3.claim: Qatada calls the pen a tremendous blessing from God, without which life would not be established or made sound.
TAB:96:3/r3.anchor: عن قتادة ( اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ الّذِي خَلَقَ ) قرأ حتى بلغ عَلّمَ بِالقَلَمِ قال :  القلم :  نعمة من الله عظيمة

TAB:96:3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r4.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r4.claim: Aisha recounts true dreams, Muhammad's retreat at Hira, Gabriel's arrival and repeated command to read, and identifies these opening verses as the first revelation.
TAB:96:3/r4.anchor: عن عائشة أنها قالت :  كان أوّل ما ابتدىء به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة

TAB:96:3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r5.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r5.claim: In Aisha's report, Khadija reassures Muhammad by citing his virtues; Waraqa identifies the revelation as Moses' angel, predicts opposition, and vows support if alive.
TAB:96:3/r5.anchor: فَقَالَتْ :  أبْشِرْ ،   فَوَاللّهِ لا يُخْزيكَ اللّهُ أبَدا ،   وَوَاللّهِ إنّكَ لَتَصِلُ الرّحَمِ

TAB:96:3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r6.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r6.claim: Aisha's account says that after Iqra the next revelations included Nun, the Pen, al-Muddaththir, and al-Duha.
TAB:96:3/r6.anchor: ثُمّ كانَ أوّلُ ما نَزَلَ عَليّ مِنَ القُرآنِ بَعْدَ «اقْرأْ » :  ( ن والقَلَمِ وَما يَسْطُرُونَ

TAB:96:3/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
TAB:96:3/r7.claim: Ibn Shaddad reports Gabriel's reading of the opening passage, Khadija's reassurance and referral to Waraqa, then delayed revelation and al-Duha's reassurance.
TAB:96:3/r7.anchor: حدثنا عبد الله بن شدّاد ،   قال :  أتى جبريل محمدا ،   فقال :  يا محمد اقرأ

TAB:96:3/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r8.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r8.claim: Aisha, through ʿUrwa and al-Zuhri, is cited as saying the first thing revealed was ‘Read in the name of your Lord who created.’
TAB:96:3/r8.anchor: عن عائشة قال إبراهيم :  قال سفيان :  حفظه لنا ابن إسحاق :  إن أوّل شيء أُنزل من القرآن :  اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:3/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r9.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r9.claim: A further report from Aisha says the first surah revealed was Iqra bi-smi rabbika.
TAB:96:3/r9.anchor: عن عائشة ،   أنّ أوّل سورة أُنزلت من القرآن اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:3/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r10.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
TAB:96:3/r10.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr says the first surah sent down to the Messenger was Iqra bi-smi rabbika alladhi khalaq.
TAB:96:3/r10.anchor: عن عُبيد بن عُمير ،   قال :  أوّل سورة نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اقرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:3/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r11.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
TAB:96:3/r11.claim: Abu Raja says he learned Iqra from Abu Musa al-Ashʿari and identifies it as Muhammad's first revealed surah.
TAB:96:3/r11.anchor: أبو رجاء العُطارديّ ،   قال :  كنا في المسجد الجامع ،   ومقرئنا أبو موسى الأشعريّ

TAB:96:3/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r12.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
TAB:96:3/r12.claim: ʿAta ibn Yasar says Iqra was the first surah revealed from the Qur'an.
TAB:96:3/r12.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار ،   قال :  أوّل سورة نزلت من القرآن اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:3/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r13.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:96:3/r13.claim: Mujahid says Iqra was the first Qur'anic revelation; one transmission adds that Nun and the Pen followed.
TAB:96:3/r13.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   قال :  أوّل ما نزل من القرآن :  اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ وزاد ابن مهديّ :  ن والْقَلَمِ

TAB:96:4/r2.speaker: author
TAB:96:4/r2.claim: Teaching by the pen means teaching creation writing and script.
TAB:96:4/r2.anchor: الّذِي عَلّمَ بِالقَلَمِ :  خَلْقَه الكتاب والخط
