IBNKATHIR:96:4/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:4/r5.claim: Ibn Kathīr adds, with the qualifier “as has reached us,” that after Waraqa's death revelation paused and grief brought Muhammad repeatedly to mountain peaks, where Gabriel reassured him he was truly God's messenger.
IBNKATHIR:96:4/r5.anchor: وفَتَر الوحي فترة حتى حَزن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم - فيما بلغنا -

IBNKATHIR:96:4/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:4/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:4/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr says the report is transmitted in both Ṣaḥīḥs through al-Zuhrī; he notes that he examined its chain, text, and meanings in his Bukhārī commentary.
IBNKATHIR:96:4/r6.anchor: وهذا الحديث مخرج في الصحيحين من حديث الزهري

IBNKATHIR:96:4/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:4/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:4/r7.claim: Ibn Kathīr says these opening verses are God's first mercy to humanity and His first blessing upon them.
IBNKATHIR:96:4/r7.anchor: وهُنَّ أول رحمة رَحم الله بها العباد

IBNKATHIR:96:4/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:4/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:4/r10.claim: Knowledge occurs mentally, orally, and in writing; written knowledge entails both mental and oral forms, while neither mental nor oral knowledge necessarily entails writing.

IBNKATHIR:96:4/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:4/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:4/r11.claim: An unnamed athar urges people to preserve knowledge by writing it down.

IBNKATHIR:96:5/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r1.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r1.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that true dreams began revelation, then the Prophet loved solitude, worshiped at Ḥirāʾ for several nights, and Khadīja supplied his provisions.
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r1.anchor: عن عائشة قالت : أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة في النوم

IBNKATHIR:96:5/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r2.claim: ʿĀʾisha recounts Gabriel's three forceful embraces in the cave, Muhammad's repeated reply that he could not read, and Gabriel's recitation of the opening revelation; Muhammad returned trembling.
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r2.anchor: فجاءه الملك فيه فقال : اقرأ . قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR:96:5/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r3.speaker: خديجة
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r3.claim: In ʿĀʾisha's report, Khadīja reassures Muhammad that God will never disgrace him, citing his kinship ties, truthfulness, bearing burdens, hospitality, and help in adversity.
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r3.anchor: يا خديجة ، ما لي : فأخبرها الخبر وقال : " قد خشيت علي " . فقالت له : كلا أبشر فوالله لا يخزيك الله أبدا ؛ إنك لتصل الرحم

IBNKATHIR:96:5/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r4.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r4.claim: Waraqa ibn Nawfal, Khadīja's relative, was a pre-Islamic Christian who wrote Arabic and Gospel material in it; he identified the angel as the messenger sent to Moses, predicted opposition and expulsion, and promised support if alive.
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r4.anchor: فقال ورقة : هذا الناموس الذي أنزل على موسى

IBNKATHIR:96:5/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r5.claim: Ibn Kathīr adds, with the qualifier “as has reached us,” that after Waraqa's death revelation paused and grief brought Muhammad repeatedly to mountain peaks, where Gabriel reassured him he was truly God's messenger.
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r5.anchor: وفَتَر الوحي فترة حتى حَزن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم - فيما بلغنا -

IBNKATHIR:96:5/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr says the report is transmitted in both Ṣaḥīḥs through al-Zuhrī; he notes that he examined its chain, text, and meanings in his Bukhārī commentary.
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r6.anchor: وهذا الحديث مخرج في الصحيحين من حديث الزهري

IBNKATHIR:96:5/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r7.claim: Ibn Kathīr says these opening verses are God's first mercy to humanity and His first blessing upon them.
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r7.anchor: وهُنَّ أول رحمة رَحم الله بها العباد

IBNKATHIR:96:5/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r10.claim: Knowledge occurs mentally, orally, and in writing; written knowledge entails both mental and oral forms, while neither mental nor oral knowledge necessarily entails writing.

IBNKATHIR:96:5/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r11.claim: An unnamed athar urges people to preserve knowledge by writing it down.

KASHSHAF:96:4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:4/r1.claim: Teaching people what they did not know shows God's complete generosity and moves them from the darkness of ignorance to the light of knowledge.
KASHSHAF:96:4/r1.anchor: فدلّ على كمال كرمه بأنه علم عباده ما لم يعلموا ،   ونقلهم من ظلمة الجهل إلى نور العلم

KASHSHAF:96:4/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:4/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:4/r2.claim: Writing has immense benefits: it records knowledge and wisdom, preserves earlier peoples' accounts and sayings and the revealed books, and sustains religious and worldly affairs.
KASHSHAF:96:4/r2.anchor: ونبه على فضل علم الكتابة لما فيه من المنافع العظيمة التي لا يحيط بها إلا هو

KASHSHAF:96:4/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:4/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:4/r3.claim: The pen and script alone suffice as evidence of God's subtle wisdom and fine ordering.
KASHSHAF:96:4/r3.anchor: ولو لم يكن على دقيق حكمة الله ولطيف تدبيره ودليل إلا أمر القلم والخط ،   لكفى به

KASHSHAF:96:4/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:4/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:4/r4.claim: An unnamed poet's couplets picture the writing instruments as black-legged figures whose motion begins when white blades play upon them, praising the pen's work.
KASHSHAF:96:4/r4.anchor: ولبعضهم في صفة القلم : وَرَوَاقِمُ رُقْشٍ كَمِثْلِ أَرَاقِم

KASHSHAF:96:4/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:4/r5.speaker: ابن الزبير
KASHSHAF:96:4/r5.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr read, “He taught writing with the pen.”

KASHSHAF:96:5/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:5/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:5/r1.claim: Teaching people what they did not know shows God's complete generosity and moves them from the darkness of ignorance to the light of knowledge.
KASHSHAF:96:5/r1.anchor: فدلّ على كمال كرمه بأنه علم عباده ما لم يعلموا ،   ونقلهم من ظلمة الجهل إلى نور العلم

KASHSHAF:96:5/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:5/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:5/r2.claim: Writing preserves sciences, wisdom, earlier peoples' reports and sayings, and revealed books; without it, religion and worldly affairs could not be properly sustained.
KASHSHAF:96:5/r2.anchor: وما دوّنت العلوم ،   ولا قيدت الحكم ،   ولا ضبطت أخبار الأولين ومقالاتهم

KASHSHAF:96:5/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:5/r4.speaker: ابن الزبير
KASHSHAF:96:5/r4.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr's reading specifies that God taught writing with the pen.

MAWARDI:96:4/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:4/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:4/r1.claim: God taught the writer to write with the pen.
MAWARDI:96:4/r1.anchor: أي علم الكاتب أن يكتب بالقلم ،   وسمي قلماً لأنه يقلم ،

MAWARDI:96:4/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:4/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:4/r2.claim: Qalam is named from the verb meaning to cut, as in trimming a fingernail.
MAWARDI:96:4/r2.anchor: وسمي قلماً لأنه يقلم ،   أي : يقطع ،   ومنه تقليم الظفر

MAWARDI:96:4/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:4/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
MAWARDI:96:4/r3.claim: Mujāhid reports from Ibn ʿUmar that God created four things with His hand and told the rest of creation to be: the pen, Throne, Garden of Eden, and Adam.
MAWARDI:96:4/r3.anchor: وروى مجاهد عن ابن عمر قال : خلق الله تعالى أربعة أشياء بيده ،   ثم قال لسائر الخلق : كن ،   فكان القلم والعرش وجنة عدن وآدم

MAWARDI:96:4/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:4/r4.speaker: كعب الأحبار
MAWARDI:96:4/r4.claim: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār says the person taught by the pen was Adam, the first to write.
MAWARDI:96:4/r4.anchor: أحدها : أنه أراد آدم عليه السلام ،   لأنه أول من كتب ،   قاله كعب الأحبار

MAWARDI:96:4/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:4/r5.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI:96:4/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies him as Idrīs, the first to write.
MAWARDI:96:4/r5.anchor: الثاني : إدريس ،   وهو أول من كتب ،   قاله الضحاك

MAWARDI:96:4/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:4/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:4/r6.claim: Māwardī also says this means everyone who writes, since all writing is learned through God's teaching; this joins the blessings of creation and instruction.
MAWARDI:96:4/r6.anchor: الثالث : أنه أراد كل من كتب بالقلم ؛ لأنه ما علم إلا بتعليم الله له

NASAFI:96:4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:4/r1.claim: God taught writing by means of the pen.

QURTUBI:96:4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:4/r1.claim: The pen means script and writing: God taught humans to write with a pen.
QURTUBI:96:4/r1.anchor: " الذي علم بالقلم " يعني الخط والكتابة ، أي علم الإنسان الخط بالقلم .

QURTUBI:96:4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:4/r2.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI:96:4/r2.claim: Qatada says, as transmitted by Said, that the pen is a great divine blessing; without it religion would not stand and life would not be sound.
QURTUBI:96:4/r2.anchor: وروى سعيد عن قتادة قال : القلم نعمة من الله تعالى عظيمة ،

QURTUBI:96:4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:4/r3.claim: The pen displays God's complete generosity: teaching people what they did not know and moving them from ignorance's darkness to knowledge's light.
QURTUBI:96:4/r3.anchor: فدل على كمال كرمه سبحانه ، بأنه علم عباده ما لم يعلموا ، ونقلهم

QURTUBI:96:4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:4/r4.claim: Writing records knowledge, preserves wisdom and earlier reports, and transmits revealed books; without it the affairs of religion and worldly life would not remain sound.
QURTUBI:96:4/r4.anchor: وما دونت العلوم ، ولا قيدت الحكم ، ولا ضبطت أخبار الأولين ومقالاتهم

QURTUBI:96:4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:4/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:4/r5.claim: The pen is called qalam because it cuts, as in trimming a fingernail.
QURTUBI:96:4/r5.anchor: وسمي قلما لأنه يقلم ، أي يقطع ، ومنه تقليم الظفر .

QURTUBI:96:4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:4/r6.claim: A modern poet likens the ink-stained pen tip to an old man courting a young woman and says it raises written pages to God.
QURTUBI:96:4/r6.anchor: وقال بعض الشعراء المحدثين يصف القلم : فكأنه والحبر يخضب رأسه

QURTUBI:96:4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:4/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
QURTUBI:96:4/r7.claim: Ibn Umar asked the Prophet whether he should write the hadith he heard; the Prophet said yes, since God taught by the pen.
QURTUBI:96:4/r7.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن عمر قال : يا رسول الله ، أأكتب ما أسمع منك

QURTUBI:96:4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:4/r8.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI:96:4/r8.claim: Mujahid reports from Abu Umar that God created four things with His hand, then told the other animals to be: the pen, Throne, Garden of Eden, and Adam.
QURTUBI:96:4/r8.anchor: وروى مجاهد عن أبي عمر قال : خلق الله عز وجل أربعة أشياء بيده

QURTUBI:96:4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:4/r9.speaker: كعب الأحبار
QURTUBI:96:4/r9.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar says the one taught by the pen is Adam, the first to write.
QURTUBI:96:4/r9.anchor: أحدها : أنه آدم عليه السلام ؛ لأنه أول من كتب ، قاله كعب الأحبار .

QURTUBI:96:4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:4/r10.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI:96:4/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak says the one taught by the pen is Idris, the first to write.
QURTUBI:96:4/r10.anchor: الثاني : أنه إدريس ، وهو أول من كتب . قاله الضحاك .

QURTUBI:96:4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:4/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:4/r11.claim: A third view includes everyone who writes, since all writing is taught by God; this gathers His favors in creating and teaching humanity.
QURTUBI:96:4/r11.anchor: الثالث : أنه أدخل كل من كتب بالقلم ؛ لأنه ما علم إلا بتعليم الله سبحانه

QURTUBI:96:4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:4/r12.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI:96:4/r12.claim: A sound report from Abu Hurayra says God wrote in a book held above the Throne that His mercy overcomes His wrath.
QURTUBI:96:4/r12.anchor: صح عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من حديث أبي هريرة ، قال : ( لما خلق الله الخلق

QURTUBI:96:4/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:4/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:96:4/r13.claim: A report established from the Prophet says the first created thing was the pen; God commanded it to write what would occur through the Resurrection, kept in the Record above His Throne.
QURTUBI:96:4/r13.anchor: وثبت عنه عليه السلام أنه قال : ( أول ما خلق الله : القلم ، فقال له اكتب

QURTUBI:96:4/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:4/r14.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI:96:4/r14.claim: An authentic report from Ibn Masud says that after forty-two nights an angel shapes the embryo, creates its faculties, and writes its sex, term, and provision according to God's decree; the angel leaves with the page, and the verse names the recording guardians.
QURTUBI:96:4/r14.anchor: وفي الصحيح من حديث ابن مسعود : أنه

QURTUBI:96:4/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:4/r15.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI:96:4/r15.claim: Scholars distinguish three pens: God's first pen, commanded to write; angels' pens for decrees, events, and deeds; and human pens for speech and practical needs.
QURTUBI:96:4/r15.anchor: قال علماؤنا : فالأقلام في الأصل ثلاثة : القلم الأول : الذي خلقه الله بيده

QURTUBI:96:4/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:4/r16.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI:96:4/r16.claim: Scholars say writing has many virtues and belongs to البيان, a form of expression particular to human beings.
QURTUBI:96:4/r16.anchor: وفي الكتابة فضائل جمة . والكتابة من جملة البيان ، والبيان مما اختص به الآدمي .

QURTUBI:96:4/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:4/r17.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI:96:4/r17.claim: Scholars say Arabs knew writing little, and Muhammad least of all; being kept from it strengthened his miracle and proof, as discussed in al-Ankabut.
QURTUBI:96:4/r17.anchor: قال علماؤنا : كانت العرب أقل الخلق معرفة بالكتاب ، وأقل العرب معرفة به المصطفى

QURTUBI:96:4/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:4/r18.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI:96:4/r18.claim: A report attributed through Ibn Masud to the Prophet says not to house women in upper rooms or teach them writing; al-Qurtubi does not state a grading.
QURTUBI:96:4/r18.anchor: وروى حماد بن سلمة عن الزبير بن عبد السلام ، عن أيوب بن عبد الله الفهري

QURTUBI:96:4/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:4/r19.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI:96:4/r19.claim: Scholars explain the warning against upper rooms by saying women might look out at men, creating temptation rather than concealment; they cite the saying that women are best off unseen by men and not seeing men.
QURTUBI:96:4/r19.anchor: قال علماؤنا : وإنما حذرهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذلك ، لأن في إسكانهن الغرف

QURTUBI:96:4/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:4/r20.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:4/r20.claim: Al-Qurtubi says writing may enable women to correspond with men they desire; writing acts as an eye for the absent and a trace of the hand, voicing thoughts beyond speech, so the Prophet sought to cut off temptation and protect hearts.
QURTUBI:96:4/r20.anchor: وكذلك تعليم الكتابة ربما كانت سببا للفتنة ، وذلك إذا علمت الكتابة كتبت إلى من تهوى

RAZI:96:4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:96:4/r1.claim: Teaching by the pen points to revealed rulings known only through transmitted teaching: the first description indicates lordship, the second prophecy; lordship can be known without prophecy, but prophecy needs lordship.
RAZI:96:4/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى الأحكام المكتوبة التي لا سبيل إلى معرفتها إلا بالسمع

RAZI:96:4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:96:4/r2.claim: One reading takes the pen as a metonym for writing, through which absent matters become known.
RAZI:96:4/r2.anchor: المراد من القلم الكتابة التي تعرف بها الأمور الغائبة

RAZI:96:4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:4/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:96:4/r3.claim: A second reading is that God taught humanity to write books with the pen; both readings emphasize the excellence of writing.
RAZI:96:4/r3.anchor: أن المراد علم الإنسان الكتاب بالقلم

RAZI:96:4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:4/r4.speaker: سليمان عليه السلام
RAZI:96:4/r4.claim: A report says Solomon asked an ifrit what speech is; the ifrit called it a passing wind, then identified writing as what binds it.
RAZI:96:4/r4.anchor: سليمان عليه السلام سأل عفريتا عن الكلام

RAZI:96:4/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:4/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:96:4/r5.claim: Rāzī praises the pen as a hunter of knowledge whose movement preserves learning through the passing nights and days.

RAZI:96:4/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:4/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:96:4/r6.claim: Like Zechariah’s quiet prayer that is heard, the silent pen reaches east and west: it does not speak, yet its message is heard far away.
RAZI:96:4/r6.anchor: قول زكريا : { إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا }

RAZI:96:4/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:4/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:96:4/r7.claim: Writing can stand in for speech across the world, but speech cannot replace writing; Rāzī compares the pen’s relation to the tongue with earth’s role as a purifying substitute.
RAZI:96:4/r7.anchor: فإن القلم ينوب عن اللسان واللسان لا ينوب عن القلم
